head: 8fa491efedb19a4bb0da7aa97ab1363b4db74021

non_issues.claim: write_private replaces a symlink that already sits at the target instead of refusing it, contradicting 'never through a symlink' / the spec's 'refused, not followed'
non_issues.why_not: The security property is that no write goes through the link, and os.replace swaps the link itself for the new file, which the module docstring states (jarvis/private_write.py:14-15). The acceptance test accepts either outcome ('refusing (raising) or replacing the link are both fine', tests/private_writes_check.py:483) and checks the link's target is untouched; it passes for all five writers. The spec's acceptance text (docs/plans/2026-10-18-security-fix-specs.md:325-326) literally says an existing symlink at the target 'is refused, not followed'. Replacing it departs from that wording but is not a security defect: a finding that only cites the wording is a nit, and one claiming a write through the link is invalid.

non_issues.claim: No fsync of the parent directory after os.replace, so a crash can lose the rename (and with it Spotify's rotated refresh token)
non_issues.why_not: Not part of the specified recipe (bytes, 0600, O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, fsync, os.replace, unlink on failure: docs/plans/2026-10-18-security-fix-specs.md:277-278), which is the recipe browser/host._write_private already used. No writer fsynced the directory before, and the old spotify _store did not fsync the file at all, so durability only improved.

non_issues.claim: The Discord token's parent directory is created with the default mode (not 0700), so the credential is exposed
non_issues.why_not: Unchanged by the diff, and the helper deliberately leaves the folder to the caller (jarvis/private_write.py:19-20). The token file itself is created 0600 from its first byte, which is the SEC-4 goal (docs/plans/2026-10-18-security-fix-specs.md:265-266); discord.mode_never_wider passes.

non_issues.claim: Removing `import uuid` from subagents.py, `import os` from spotify_auth.py or the inline recipe from host.py breaks remaining uses (NameError)
non_issues.why_not: grep on the head finds no remaining uuid. use in subagents.py and no os. use in spotify_auth.py; host.py keeps its os import for other code. All 36 private_writes_check cases and browser_host_activity_check pass.

non_issues.claim: subagents._compact now builds the whole snapshot in memory instead of streaming lines to the descriptor, which can blow up memory
non_issues.why_not: The compacted file is bounded by what the thread holds, at most THREAD_BYTES of entries (docstring at subagents.py:649-652), and the old code serialised the same lines anyway. Errors are still swallowed and logged as before.

non_issues.claim: stt_settings.update now writes different bytes (json.dumps vs json.dump to a text handle) or a different temp name, changing the settings file
non_issues.why_not: json.dumps(current, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n' encoded as UTF-8 is byte-identical to the old json.dump with the same arguments plus write('\n') (ensure_ascii defaults to True in both), and the temp name shape .<name>.<hex8>.tmp and flags are the ones the old inline recipe used. The spec allows the switch (docs/plans/2026-10-18-security-fix-specs.md:281-282).

non_issues.claim: Spotify's rotated refresh token is no longer guaranteed to be on disk before the new access token is returned
non_issues.why_not: _store (now write_private) still runs synchronously, inside the lock, before _cached_token is set and returned; write_private completes fsync and os.replace before returning. tests/private_writes_check.py spotify.rotated_persisted_before_use passes.

non_issues.claim: A random 32-bit temp suffix can collide and O_EXCL then fails the write
non_issues.why_not: A collision needs a leftover or concurrent temp with the same 8 hex digits beside the same target; failures are cleaned up (no leftovers), and on that vanishing chance O_EXCL fails closed (an error, never a shared or followed file), which the callers already handle (spotify swallows OSError, subagents logs).

notes: Verified clean. private_writes_check 36/36 and browser_host_activity_check 10/10 pass on the head; the PR body reports 18 of 36 failing on main. All three claimed defects (Discord/Google write-then-chmod, Spotify fixed .tmp) are fixed through the helper; every brief claim matches the diff.
